title: WebMapX Layer Repository — Harvest Source
description: A curated pointer to somewhere layers can be read from automatically. This is the hand-maintained part of the catalog: reviewing one means judging whether an endpoint is worth trusting, which a person can do — as opposed to eyeballing the thousands of layer records it yields, which nobody can. Everything downstream is generated into harvested/ and is not in git.

type.description: How to read this source. Self-describing services (WMS/WMTS GetCapabilities, OGC API) versus third-party catalogues that already did the harvesting, of which the QGIS PDOK plugin's layer list is one.

url.description: Where to read it. A capabilities document, or the catalogue file itself.

provider.description: Who the harvested layers belong to. Read off the source rather than inferred from its hostname, because a catalogue or cache is not the provider of what it lists.

categories.description: Themes the provider's layers cover. Carried through to the harvested provider record; harvesting cannot infer it from a capabilities document.

attribution.description: Credit line every harvested layer carries, written into webmapxConfig.source.attribution. Set it when the licensor dictates the wording — CC BY licences do. {year} resolves at harvest time. Left out, one is built from the provider's name, url and licence.

search.description: How to query a catalogue source. A catalogue holds everything anybody registered, so unlike a capabilities document it has to be asked a question rather than read whole.

query.description: Full-text query, in Elasticsearch query_string syntax. Left out, every record with a renderable link is taken, subject to include.limit.

bbox.description: Only records whose extent intersects this box. Defaults to the source's bounds.

region.description: Path under layers/ the output belongs to, e.g. world/europe/netherlands

bounds.description: Geographic extent [west, south, east, north] of everything this source serves. Written onto every harvested layer, so a client can frame it: a national dataset shown at a world zoom reads as blank rather than as data. Capabilities documents carry per-layer bounding boxes, but third-party catalogues generally do not, so this is stated once here.

maintainer.description: Who keeps the source itself current. That a list is maintained by a known person is a fact about the source, not about each layer in it.

include.description: Which of the source's layers to take. A capabilities document usually offers far more than is worth publishing.

serviceTypes.description: Default: those a web map can render (wms, wmts, api tiles)

crs.description: Drop layers the service cannot deliver in this CRS

match.description: Regular expression the layer name or title must match

exclude.description: Regular expression that disqualifies a layer

limit.description: Cap on layers taken, for a first pass at a very large source

enrich.description: Set false to skip legend and attribute enrichment for this source. Attribute schemas cost one request per layer, so a service offering tens of thousands of layers is left unenriched rather than hammered on every harvest.

expandStyles.description: Set false to keep a layer with several published WMS styles as one layer. Default is to expand: a style is a different rendering of the same source, which is what a layer is.

liveSearch.description: Whether the previewer may search this catalogue from the browser. False where the deployment refuses CORS preflight, which makes the search impossible from a page while leaving the harvest unaffected — offering it anyway is a control that cannot work. Verify with an OPTIONS request carrying Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method before setting it true.
liveSearch.$comment: Only meaningful for catalogue source types.
